chunks: Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a man while we were with him, and it was said to him: he has died. So he invoked mercy for him and spoke well of him.

Then a man from the people said: he owed me a few dinars, and he overpowered me regarding them, and he described them as insignificant. He said: that became visible in the face of Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, and he said: “Do you think Allah would seize a devotee of Ali عليه السلام and cast him into the Fire and punish him because of your gold?”
He said: so the man said, “He is absolved of it; may Allah make me your ransom.” Then Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: “Why was that not before now?”

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, meaning divine punishment in the Hereafter
key_terms.تَرَحَّمَ: he invoked Allah's mercy upon the deceased
key_terms.دُنَيْنِيرَاتٌ: a few small dinars; a minor monetary amount
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: released from liability; pardoned and absolved
key_terms.وَلِيَّ عَلِيٍّ: a devotee and loyal follower of Ali عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about forgiving a deceased believer's small debt?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the ethical importance of pardoning small debts, especially after a person's death, and it condemns insistence on trivial worldly claims in a way that harms the believer. It also reflects the sanctity of the wilayah of Amir al-Mu'minin Ali عليه السلام and the gravity of exposing a deceased believer over minor financial grievances.
